# PROCESS — cand_0002 (parent cand_0001, val 0.653)

Diagnosed EVERY failing/flaky task in THIS iteration's `./trajectories/` with 5 parallel
read-only subagents (one per group), plus verified the recalc mechanism from source
(`third_party/spreadsheetbench/evaluation/open_spreadsheet.py`): before grading the harness
runs **LibreOffice headless** to recalc formulas, then the scorer loads `data_only=True`. So a
live `=formula` IS evaluated and can pass — CONFIRMED by passing tasks 46897 (COUNTIF), 55060
(IF), 58109 (SUMIFS). This overturns the parent prompt's claim that "the grader may not
recalculate formulas reliably."

## Ranked clusters (leverage = #tasks × trials × recoverable score)
| rank | cluster | tasks | root cause | tag | lever |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Hidden-input over-fit | 39046, 51359, 30709, 59667, 38332 | Code reproduces the visible sample but bakes in a no-op condition / hardcoded extent / answer-range-derived bound / stale cached spill | KNOWLEDGE (generalization) | new "runs on three inputs" section w/ concrete traps |
| 2 | Ignore existing formula pattern | 56637, 11842 | Invented ad-hoc logic instead of extending a formula already in/adjacent to the answer range | KNOWLEDGE + structure | "replicate the existing formula" bullet |
| 3 | Formula won't recalc | 55667, 47741 | Used `AGGREGATE`/dynamic-array/`_xlfn.` prefix + `IFERROR(...,"")` mask → blank after LibreOffice recalc | CONTRACT/CONFLICT | function-compatibility guard |
| 4 | Hardcoded literal vs formula-GT | 57090, 57232 | Hardcoded a Python value that diverges from Excel-specific evaluation (FREQUENCY ignores text; INDEX/MATCH alignment) | CONFLICT (decision) | consolidate literal-vs-formula decision; correct false recalc claim |

## Edits (all in prompt.md) + lever + verify + blast radius
1. **New section "Your code runs on three different inputs — make it general"** (KNOWLEDGE).
   Traps: implement every stated condition even if the sample makes it a no-op & apply it to the
   SOURCE set; derive extents dynamically; never read a threshold/bound/which-cells from the answer
   range; coerce types & lock parse convention from examples; recompute spill/array results from raw
   source, don't fabricate blanks.
   - Verify: 39046 counts SUBREFs over ALL rows, gating only the output row on CANCELLED (sample is
     all-CANCELLED) → rule "apply each filter to the source set" makes it exclude non-CANCELLED source
     rows. 51359 hardcodes `range(1,15)` → "derive extents dynamically". 59667 t1 clamps to `min/max`
     of pre-filled D values → "never read a bound from the answer range". 38332 trusts cached UNIQUE
     spill / fabricates blanks → "recompute from raw source, don't fabricate".
   - Blast radius: **BOUNDED** — additive knowledge. The 29 passing tasks already generalize (they
     pass all 3 hidden inputs), so none change behavior.
2. **"Match the examples" — new bullet: extend an existing in-range/adjacent formula** (KNOWLEDGE+structure).
   - Verify: 56637's answer range B12:B60 already holds `=IF(ROWS($A$12:A12)>$B$5,...)`; agent invented
     a different `AND(ROW()...)` formula → rule "extend the SAME formula" fills it down. 11842's A5:I12
     already holds the yearly-total formula pattern; agent invented an aggregation → replicate instead.
   - Blast radius: **BOUNDED** — conditional on an existing formula being present. A passing task that
     writes literals into an empty range is untouched; if a passing task had an adjacent formula it
     already matched, the equivalent fill recalcs to the same value.
3. **Rework "Writing values correctly" + new "Literal value vs. live formula"** (CONSOLIDATION of a
   contradicted claim + additive function guard). Removed the false "grader may not recalculate
   formulas reliably"; stated recalc happens (LibreOffice); made the choice conditional: literal when
   derivable unambiguously in Python; formula when asked-for / already-present / Excel-specific
   semantics. Added: only widely-supported functions; avoid `AGGREGATE`/dynamic-array/`XLOOKUP`/
   `FILTER`/`LET`/`TEXTJOIN`; strip `_xlfn.` prefix; no masking `IFERROR(...,"")`.
   - Verify: 55667 t0 (SUMPRODUCT/INDEX) passed, t1 (`AGGREGATE(15,6,.../array)`) → blank → 0/3;
     guard steers to SUMPRODUCT. 47741 wrote `=_xlfn.TEXTJOIN(...)` (unparseable prefix + avoided
     func) → guard forbids both. 57090/57232 hardcoded literals diverging from a FREQUENCY / INDEX-MATCH
     GT → corrected decision makes writing the sheet's formula the intended path.
   - Blast radius: this touches the GLOBAL literal-vs-formula decision, so borderline **UNBOUNDED** —
     checked the whole class: the 3 passing formula tasks use COUNTIF/IF/SUMIFS (all on the supported
     list, none on the avoid list) → unchanged/reinforced; passing literal-writers keep writing literals
     ("derive unambiguously in Python"), and any equivalent formula would recalc to the same value they
     already match. The function guard prevents the only regression path (writing an unsupported func).
     No passing task's action flips.
4. **Pre-finish checklist items (4) generality and (5) supported-function/existing-formula** — makes
   edits 1–3 verifiable at finish time (structure, not new rules).

## VERIFIED unwinnable / not-prose-fixable (diagnosed, NOT edited)
- 56996: gold looks up cells filled with volatile `RANDBETWEEN`; agent's formula == GT but recalc
  redraws fresh randoms → cannot match. Unwinnable.
- 325-44, 450-9: ground-truth `*_answer.xlsx` produced by a buggy reference macro that contradicts
  BOTH the instruction and the workbook's own demo tab (325-44: careType column = literal `'careType'`
  + empty cell = `' '`; 450-9: spurious `'E'` label above a header shifted to row 3). Data-quality
  defects; agent's instruction-faithful output is correct. Not prose-fixable.
- 5192: the two worked examples are mutually inconsistent (`CH02A1456`→drops `A`; `MH2A215`→keeps it).
  55931: column E has no worked example — sign convention & non-match representation undetermined.
  59743: GT ADDS J where the instruction says "difference" (subtract). 50630: agent's logic already
  reproduces the visible example; residual failure is brittle exact-whitespace reproduction on hidden
  inputs. 59259/56427: residual task-specific aggregation/type edges. Left alone — no reliable general
  prose fix; chasing them risks over-fitting.

## Process & features
- 5 parallel `general-purpose` subagents for read-only diagnosis; verified recalc + scorer from source.
  No worktrees (single prose file). Built on cand_0001 (ACCEPTED). Did NOT re-touch the parent's
  example-matching/type-contract rules that fixed 110-2/3911/50051/51958/73-45/CF_11072.

## Preserve
- The verified grading facts (type-equalization; only values graded; recalc via LibreOffice for
  supported functions). "Match the pre-filled examples" remains the single highest-leverage rule.

## Deliberately skipped
- Above unwinnable set. Did NOT re-introduce cand_0001's `broke={55667}` change verbatim — instead I
  DIAGNOSED why 55667 regressed (AGGREGATE non-recalc) and added the function-compatibility guard that
  redirects it to the SUMPRODUCT form its own passing trial used.
